data.name: Ramratan
data.gender_notes: Ramratan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ram means God and Ratan means grace or jewel. This name signifies the blessings and grace of God, and the person is believed to be protected and blessed by the divine. The name Ramratan carries the meaning “God's grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ramratan usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ramratan is a devotional name, often used for boys who are believed to be blessed by Lord Rama. The name signifies the presence of God's grace in one's life and the protection and blessings of the deity.
data.etymology: Ramratan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ramratan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Ramratan" holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is derived from the name of Lord Rama, a major deity and an embodiment of the supreme self and the perfect man. The name resonates with the Vedic ideals of dharma (duty), artha (prosperity), kama (desire), and moksha (liberation) – the four fundamental objectives of human life in Hindu philosophy.
data.spiritual_significance: "Ramratan" evokes a deep spiritual significance by reminding the bearer of the divine name and presence of Lord Rama. This name is considered a powerful invocation of the grace and protection of the deity. In Hindu devotional practice, saying the name of God is believed to purify the mind and soul and bring the individual closer to ultimate truth and enlightenment. Hence this name is often given to a child as a blessings, wishing him or her the blessings, grace and protection of Lord Rama.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ramratan: The embodiment of Lord Rama's grace and divine blessings. A name that echoes the inner sanctum of devotion and love, reminding the bearer to uphold righteousness and virtue in life.

historical_references.reference:
Ramchandra was a popular king of the Solar Dynasty in ancient India around 3000 BCE. He is said to have built the ancient city of Ayodhya and established the Ikshvaku dynasty. Ramratan is believed to be a revered deity and son of Ramchandra, and is often depicted with a mace in his hand.
Context: Mythological and Historical References.

During the medieval period, Ramratan was an important deity in the Hindu Vaishnavism sect, particularly in western India. He is often depicted with four arms and four faces, each representing different aspects of Vishnu.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Ramratan' has seen a modern resurgence in various cultural contexts. In the realm of devotional music, 'Ramratan' is a popular name for compositions dedicated to Lord Rama, who is a central figure in Hindu mythology. These compositions can be found on music streaming platforms such as Spotify and YouTube. On Instagram, 'Ramratan' is also used as a personal name by some individuals who wish to express their spiritual or cultural identity. This trend reflects the growing popularity of Hinduism and its rich cultural heritage in the modern world.
